documents.title: Claims ledger: the audit's written record
Terms acceptance: wording, links and record

claims.quote: Provisioning job logs: 30 days by default.

evidence.shows: The published default window for job logs is 30 days.
The collector reads its default window from that same constant.
The collector passes that window to the SQL function that deletes.

evidence.pattern: FUNCTION public\.gc_job_logs\(\s*p_age INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '30 days'
evidence.shows: The SQL function's own default is also 30 days.

claims.quote: Removed cloud inventory and capability observations: 7 days by default.

evidence.shows: The sweep's default window is 7 days, overridable by one environment variable.
Removed inventory rows are purged with that window.
Removed capability observations are purged with the same window.

claims.quote: {CONSENT_COOKIE_NAME}: records the analytics choice, the policy version, and the decision time for 183 days.

evidence.shows: The cookie's lifetime is 183 days.
That lifetime is what the cookie is written with.
The record holds the policy version and the decision time beside the choice.
The name the browser holds.
The name the page prints is the same string.

claims.quote: There is exactly one optional choice — product analytics — and it is off until you turn it on.

evidence.shows: The consent record carries one optional choice.
With no stored record the answer is no.
Without that answer the console does not load the analytics SDK.
The SDK itself starts opted out.

claims.quote: if your browser sends the GPC signal, optional analytics stays off and the stored choice cannot override it

evidence.shows: The signal is read before the stored choice and wins over it.
The console asks for that combined answer, not for the stored field.

claims.quote: the analytics SDK is configured so that recording cannot start.

evidence.shows: The SDK is initialised with recording disabled.

claims.quote: Paid plans are billed through Stripe, which acts as our payment processor.

evidence.shows: Stripe is in the processing register as an active party, so the subprocessors page lists it.
The console depends on the Stripe SDK.

claims.quote: The company is not registered for VAT.

evidence.shows: The entity record says the company is not registered for VAT.

claims.quote: Transactional email is delivered through Amazon Web Services (Amazon SES) in its Frankfurt, Germany region (eu-central-1).

evidence.shows: The hosted deploy sends through SES unless the vault names another transport.
The deploy refuses a vault that still names Resend.
The SES account the hosted service sends from is in eu-central-1.
The processing register records SES as active, so the subprocessors page lists it.

claims.requires: The value of EMAIL_PROVIDER in the production vault. Unset and ses both mean SES, and the deploy refuses resend; but the vault may name smtp, the rollback transport, and while it does the statement is false.

claims.quote: > I have read and accept the Terms of Service (version 2026-08-24).

evidence.shows: The label opens with the shared constant the e2e fixture locates the box by.
The module builds the label from that prefix followed by "the".
Each document title is followed by its version in brackets.
The Terms of Service are sealed at version 2026-08-24, the version the example prints.

claims.quote: > How we use your personal data is explained in our Privacy Policy.

evidence.pattern: noticeBefore: "How we use your personal data is explained in our ",
evidence.shows: The notice line opens with these words and is followed by the Privacy Policy link.
The notice line links the Privacy Policy.
The Privacy Policy is not an acceptance-required document, so the box does not cover it.

claims.quote: The accepted set is every document in `LEGAL_DOCUMENTS` with `acceptanceRequired: true`.

evidence.shows: The module derives the accepted set from the registry flag.
The server action records only acceptance-required documents.

claims.quote: The version and the hash are copied in, never looked up later.

evidence.shows: The server action writes the sealed version and hash from the registry into the row it inserts.
The module names the same two registry values for the same documents.

claims.quote: `signup` if the person never accepted any version of the document before, otherwise `reacceptance`

evidence.shows: The context is signup for a first acceptance and reacceptance otherwise.
First acceptance is decided per document from the stored rows, not from client input.

claims.quote: Submitting twice does not add a second row for the same version.

evidence.shows: An existing row for the same person, document and version skips the insert.

claims.quote: Links use the instance's legal address (`legalUrl`, which reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_LEGAL_URL`)

evidence.shows: The module resolves links through legalUrl by default.
legalUrl reads NEXT_PUBLIC_LEGAL_URL.

claims.quote: Social sign-in may come from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Google. Email sign-in uses a one-time code.

evidence.shows: GitHub sign-in is configured from its client id and secret.
Google sign-in likewise.
GitLab sign-in likewise.
Bitbucket sign-in likewise; these four are the only social providers.
Email sign-in is Better Auth's one-time-code plugin.

claims.quote: the payment fields are Stripe-hosted, so card numbers do not pass through our systems

evidence.shows: The card form is Stripe's Payment Element, which Stripe.js mounts in its own frame.
The payment forms are wrapped in Stripe Elements.
The purchase path uses a Stripe Checkout session, a page Stripe serves.

claims.quote: Analytics uses internal account and organization identifiers rather than names or email addresses.

evidence.shows: The person is identified by the internal user id, with no traits.
The organization is grouped by its internal id with plan and role only.

claims.quote: We do not record sessions: there is no session replay, and no choice that could enable one.

evidence.shows: The analytics SDK is initialised with recording disabled.
The consent record has one choice, analytics; there is no replay choice.

claims.quote: If your browser sends Global Privacy Control, we honour it as a standing opt-out and optional analytics stays off

evidence.shows: The signal is read before the stored choice and wins over it.

claims.quote: Withdrawing the choice deletes the analytics provider’s identifiers and browser storage from your device.

evidence.shows: When the answer becomes no, the provider's storage is purged.

claims.quote: proportionate server and migration errors and structured operational logs may be sent to PostHog

evidence.pattern: # Structured logs → PostHog Logs over OTLP
evidence.shows: The hosted deploy points the structured-log exporter at PostHog.
And passes that endpoint to the console.
The migration runner reports to PostHog EU.

claims.quote: The primary hosted control plane, PostgreSQL database, and S3-compatible object storage run in Hetzner’s fsn1 location in Germany.

evidence.shows: The control-plane server's location defaults to fsn1.
The workflow that applies it does not override the location.
PostgreSQL runs on that server, in the production compose file.
So does the S3-compatible object store.

claims.quote: PostHog EU Cloud processes the telemetry and operational data described above.

evidence.shows: The browser SDK's host defaults to PostHog's EU ingestion.
The first-party proxy forwards only to PostHog EU.

claims.quote: Cloudflare processes edge-network and security data.

evidence.pattern: fronts the origin with a Cloudflare Tunnel
evidence.shows: The production origin is reached through a Cloudflare Tunnel.
Cloudflare is an active party in the processing register.

claims.quote: Fleet-action records: 90 days by default.

evidence.shows: The published default window for fleet actions is 90 days.
The collector reads its default from that constant.
And passes it to the SQL function that deletes.

evidence.pattern: FUNCTION public\.gc_fleet_actions\(\s*p_age INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '90 days'
evidence.shows: Whose own default is also 90 days.

claims.quote: Authorization activity records: 365 days by default.

evidence.shows: The published default window for authorization activity is 365 days.
The collector reads its default from that constant.
And passes it to the SQL function that deletes.

evidence.pattern: FUNCTION public\.gc_authz_activity_log\(\s*p_age INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '365 days'
evidence.shows: Whose own default is also 365 days.

claims.quote: Deletion from encrypted backups may occur on the backup rotation rather than immediately; restored data is re-subjected to the deletion request.

evidence.shows: The off-box copy is age-encrypted.
Copies expire on a rotation: 14 daily by default.
And 8 weekly.

evidence.pattern: this copy is what lets the restore replay it
evidence.shows: Erasure tombstones are exported hourly so a restore replays deletions made after the dump.

claims.requires: That the backup timers are installed and running on the production box. The restore drill record named in docs/ops/restore-runbook.md is the evidence; none is in the tree yet.

claims.quote: better-auth.session_token and secure-prefixed variants

evidence.shows: The session cookie's name.
Its secure-prefixed variant.

claims.quote: If you consent, the hosted Alethia service loads PostHog EU Cloud

evidence.shows: Without consent the SDK is not loaded.
The host it loads against defaults to PostHog EU.

claims.quote: We use internal identifiers and low-cardinality plan or role attributes

evidence.shows: The person is identified by the internal id only.
The organization carries plan and role and nothing else.

claims.quote: VAT registration: not registered

evidence.shows: The entity record says the company is not registered for VAT.

claims.quote: you can also ask for your account to be deleted from Delete account in your account settings.

evidence.shows: The account settings dialog has a Delete account section.
Its button calls the self-service erasure request.

evidence.pattern: It OPENS A CASE and erases nothing\.
evidence.shows: Which opens a case and deletes nothing.

claims.quote: On AWS, Google Cloud and Azure it signs in with short-lived federated credentials and stores no cloud key.

evidence.shows: AWS access is federated from Alethia's OIDC issuer; nothing is emitted for it.
Azure likewise.

evidence.pattern: # GCP needs NO separate secret either
evidence.shows: Google Cloud likewise.
The only clouds connected by a stored token are DigitalOcean, Hetzner and Civo.

claims.quote: the OpenTofu state of the infrastructure we provisioned for you

evidence.shows: The console keeps OpenTofu state in its own object-store bucket.
And serves it to runners as the state backend.

claims.quote: it also holds the token or key you gave it, encrypted at rest

evidence.shows: A token cloud's API token is encrypted before it is stored.
A connector's secret fields are encrypted before they are stored.

claims.quote: A self-service export in the console is being built and is not available yet.

evidence.shows: The self-service privacy actions do not build an export.
Settings has no export page; LEG-L3 adds one, and this entry then has to be revisited.

claims.quote: statutory accounting records, and proof of which terms your account accepted

evidence.shows: An erasure keeps the terms-acceptance record.
And the orders kept for accounting.

claims.quote: At the end of the retrieval window we delete what we hold

evidence.shows: Deletion is performed by fulfilling an erasure case.

claims.requires: A person opening and fulfilling the erasure when the 30-day retrieval window ends. Nothing in the repository schedules it, and no screen calls fulfilErasure yet (#7222).

claims.quote: has not yet opened paid plans to individuals in any country

evidence.shows: No market is open.
The sentence is shown only while no consumer cell exists.

claims.quote: You can also withdraw from the billing settings in the console, which shows what you will get back before you confirm.

evidence.shows: The billing settings page mounts the withdrawal control.
The control shows the refund the server computed before the consumer acts.

evidence.pattern: description=\{`You will be refunded \$\{refund\} and \$\{retained\} will be retained
evidence.shows: The confirm step repeats the refund and the retained amount before the withdrawal is made.

claims.quote: If we cannot refund automatically, for example because there was no card payment to refund against, we contact you within 14 days to arrange it.

evidence.pattern: if \(!refundIssued\) \{\n\t\tawait alertOperator\(\{\n\t\t\ttitle: "Withdrawal refund owed but not issued"
evidence.shows: When an owed refund could not be issued, the withdrawal action alerts the platform operator.
The acknowledgement repeats the sentence only when the refund was not issued.

claims.requires: A person acting on the operator alert: contacting the consumer and arranging the refund within 14 days of the withdrawal. Nothing in the repository schedules or tracks that contact.

claims.quote: Бутонът, с който се прави поръчката, гласи „ {CONSUMER_PAYMENT_OBLIGATION_LABEL_BG}“

evidence.shows: The Bulgarian label is the ЗЗП art. 49(2) formulation.
orderButtonLabel returns it for a consumer addressed in Bulgarian. No checkout renders orderButtonLabel yet; the consumer checkout that will is not built.

claims.quote: Encrypted at rest; never with a self-managed runner

evidence.shows: The Hetzner token is encrypted before it is stored.

evidence.pattern: the credential lives only in the customer's\s*// self-hosted runner env, never in Alethia
evidence.shows: With a self-managed runner the token stays in the customer's runner.

claims.quote: { cloud: "AWS", access: "Short-lived role assumed per job (OIDC)", stored: "Nothing"

evidence.shows: AWS access is federated; no key is held.
AWS, Google Cloud and Azure are not token clouds.

claims.quote: id: "anthropic",

evidence.shows: The assistant's default executor model is Anthropic's.
So is the default advisor.
Requests go to Anthropic with the deployment's own key, not one the customer supplies.
The hosted deploy passes that key from the vault.
The assistant stays off until the provider's evidence is recorded.

claims.requires: Whether ALETHIA_AI_ANTHROPIC_DPA, _TRANSFER, _RETENTION and _NO_TRAINING are set in the production vault. Until they are, the assistant is off and Anthropic receives nothing; the register lists it as the provider the feature uses (#7223).

claims.quote: Hosted compute, database, backups, and object storage

evidence.shows: Hetzner server backups are on for the control-plane box.

claims.quote: Processing is primarily in Germany.

evidence.shows: The control plane is in Hetzner fsn1, Germany.
Email is sent from AWS Frankfurt.

claims.quote: kept as 14 daily and 8 weekly copies by default

evidence.shows: 14 daily copies by default.
8 weekly copies by default.

claims.quote: `PAID_MARKETS` in `packages/legal/src/commerce.ts` is empty

evidence.shows: The list is empty.

claims.quote: No console or admin screen calls `openPrivacyCase`, `verifyPrivacyCaseIdentity` or `fulfilErasure` yet

evidence.shows: The only privacy-case UI imports the self-service request, not the staff steps.

findings.says: The page tells the reader the Terms were last updated on August 12, 2026.
findings.actually: The sealed version is 2026-08-24: sections 5 and 13 were changed on that date and the version was bumped for it. The date on the page was not moved, so a reader who accepts version 2026-08-24 is shown a date twelve days older.

evidence.shows: The registry's version for the Terms.

findings.quote: Art. 97a(1) imposes the same registration on a company that **receives**
findings.says: Flagged by the tax research (1 of 3). The decisions of 2026-11-17 record that a Bulgarian company needs the Art. 97a registration before its first sale to a business in another member state.
findings.actually: Correct but incomplete. The same registration is triggered by receiving a taxable service from a supplier outside Bulgaria, whether or not anything has been sold, so it may already be due; the repository cannot see the purchase invoices that decide it. The dividing line is also not organization against consumer, as PayerCapacity draws it, but whether the customer has given a VAT number.

findings.quote: "No VAT registration now" and "EU businesses" do not fit together
findings.says: Flagged by the tax research (2 of 3). The decisions of 2026-11-17 open the EU to businesses and individuals with no VAT registration now, registering on traction.
findings.actually: The two cannot both hold for a business in another member state that gives a VAT number: the Art. 97a application is due seven days before that customer is first charged, so registering once there is a customer is too late. Either the registration is filed before launch or those cells stay closed.

findings.says: Flagged by the tax research (3 of 3). The paid-markets record lists what a consumer cell needs: pre-contractual information, the payment-obligation button, the 14-day withdrawal right, durable confirmation and dispute-body information.
findings.actually: It does not list the online withdrawal function that the Consumer Rights Directive has required since 19 June 2026 (Art. 11a; Bulgarian Consumer Protection Act Art. 52a, in force 24 September 2026): a control labelled "withdraw from contract here", a confirmation step, and an acknowledgement on a durable medium. Whether the console's withdrawal flow meets those labels was not checked here.

evidence.shows: The paid-markets record does not mention the function or either article.
The tax research says so.

findings.quote: Without an OSS registration there is no return through which to report VAT collected in another member state
findings.says: The tax condition says a sale to an individual elsewhere in the EU is taxed where the customer is and needs an OSS registration to report it.
findings.actually: The tax research found that this holds only above EUR 10,000 a year of such sales across the EU. At or under that total the place of supply stays in Bulgaria, an unregistered company charges no VAT on the sale, and no OSS registration is needed. Follows from the tax research; not one of the three points it raises itself.

evidence.pattern: No OSS registration is needed, and none is possible on these facts
evidence.shows: The tax research's conclusion below the threshold.

findings.quote: Alethia does not store static cloud access keys.
findings.says: The policy says Alethia stores no static cloud access key and that cloud access uses short-lived federated credentials.
findings.actually: True for AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Alibaba Cloud only. Hetzner, DigitalOcean and Civo have no federation: the customer's scoped API token is stored, encrypted at rest, unless a self-managed runner holds it. API keys entered for connectors (DNS, registries, secret stores, observability) are stored encrypted too, and the paragraph does not mention them. The page is sealed, so the fix is the re-seal's. Proposed text: "On AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Alibaba Cloud, Alethia stores no cloud access key; access uses short-lived, federated credentials. Clouds without federation (such as Hetzner) use a scoped API token you supply, which we store encrypted at rest, or not at all when you run your own runner. API keys you enter for a connector are stored encrypted at rest." The Security and Data Act pages already say this.

evidence.shows: Three clouds are connected by a stored token.
The token is stored, encrypted.
Connector secrets are stored, encrypted.

findings.quote: support conversations, and the metadata needed to manage your environments
findings.says: Section 1 lists the infrastructure and service data Alethia processes.
findings.actually: It does not list the AI assistant: the conversations (agent_threads and related tables) and the infrastructure context sent with a prompt, which go to the model provider when the assistant is on. The erasure plan already treats AI conversations as the subject's data. The page is sealed, so the fix is the re-seal's: add "AI assistant conversations and the project context sent with them" to the list.

evidence.shows: Assistant conversations are stored.

evidence.pattern: AI conversations are the subject's own content
evidence.shows: The erasure plan names them.

findings.says: The processing register lists Hetzner for backups and no other backup recipient.
findings.actually: The nightly off-box copy is written to an S3-compatible store at a provider that is deliberately not Hetzner. The copy is encrypted before upload, but the provider is still a recipient. Its name is set on the production box, not in the repository, so it cannot be registered here until the maintainer names it (#7223).

evidence.pattern: S3-compatible, at a provider that is NOT Hetzner
evidence.shows: The off-box store is at another provider.
The register names no such provider.

findings.says: The processing register lists Cloudflare for inbound email routing.
findings.actually: Cloudflare forwards the published addresses (support, sales, legal, privacy, security) to one destination mailbox set from the vault. The provider of that mailbox receives every privacy request and support email and is not registered (#7223).

evidence.shows: privacy@ is one of the forwarded addresses.
The register names no mailbox provider.

findings.says: The processing register does not list Slack.
findings.actually: When SUPPORT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is set, each new support case and reply posts its subject, severity and organization id to a Slack webhook. Whether it is set in production is a vault fact (#7223).

evidence.shows: The case subject is posted.
The hosted deploy passes the webhook from the vault.
The register does not list Slack.
